content.text: I now have everything needed to resolve this ticket. The root cause is crystal clear.

input.note:
**Root Cause:** The `harbor-pull` image pull Secret exists in the `reporting` namespace but was **not** recreated in the new `analytics` namespace. Kubernetes Secrets are namespace-scoped — a pod can only reference image pull secrets that exist in its own namespace [cite: concepts/containers/images#creating-a-secret-with-a-docker-config-1] [cite: concepts/configuration/secret#using-imagepullsecrets-0].

**Evidence:**
- `usage-exporter-6b4d9c8f7-2vjxq` in `analytics` is in `ImagePullBackOff` with the event: *"FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret: Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (\<harbor-pull\>)"* and the error: *"failed to authorize: 401 Unauthorized"* from `harbor.acme.internal`.
- The identical pod in `reporting` (same image `harbor.acme.internal/data/usage-exporter:1.8.2`, same secret name `harbor-pull`) is `Running` fine — confirming the secret exists in `reporting` but not in `analytics` [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry#create-a-pod-that-uses-your-secret-2].

**Fix:** Copy the `harbor-pull` Secret into the `analytics` namespace. Run:
```bash
kubectl get secret harbor-pull -n reporting -o yaml \
  | sed 's/namespace: reporting/namespace: analytics/' \
  | kubectl apply -f -
```
Once the secret is present in `analytics`, the kubelet will be able to authenticate to Harbor and pull the image successfully [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry#create-a-pod-that-uses-your-secret-1].
